newsitem.title: LEBANON: HSBC to start trading on Beirut exchange mid-Aug.
newsitem.headline: HSBC to start trading on Beirut exchange mid-Aug.

text.p: HSBC will start trading on the Beirut Stock Exchange through local brokerage firms by mid-August, a company official said on Monday.

"We think it is a very good time to start. We will begin trading through local brokers in a couple of weeks, maximum by mid-August," Albert Moumdjian, head of the Middle East and North Africa desk of HSBC, told Reuters in a telephone call from London.
Moumdjian said HSBC reached the decision after a three-month study of the Lebanese market. It planned to publish a country report on Lebanon in two weeks' time.
"The decision to come in is very good for the Beirut Stock Exchange. I am bullish on banking sector and very positive on Solidere," he said.
He said HSBC looked positively upon the recent trend of big Lebanese banks acquiring smaller banks. "We see Lebanese banks as consolidating their positions not only domestically but also regionally".

Stocks of the three banks listed on the BSE have been appreciating ever since their market debuts a few months ago. Solidere have surged recently on news that the company was opening up to foreign investors.
